card werk-chat-no-card-line  [open]
A turn sent with no card open says that the map shows the whole tree
why: Every turn starts with a line about the open card, so the agent always knows what the person looks at. With no card open, a missing line would leave the agent on the card that the last turn named.

A turn sent from the map's whole tree has no open card to name. To keep the first line on every turn, the line then says that no card is open and that the map shows the whole tree. The next turn sent with a card open says that the map is now at that card, because the open card changed. See #werk-card-blind for the now-at and still-on lines.

Example:

- The whole tree: the map page with no card open.
- Card A: #werk-chat "The composer sends a live agent turn".

1. The map shows the whole tree. The person sends "What is left open?". The turn starts with [no card is open: the map shows the whole tree].
2. The person opens card A and sends a second message. The turn starts with [the map is now at #werk-chat — The composer sends a live agent turn].
3. The person sends a third message from card A. The turn starts with [still on #werk-chat — The composer sends a live agent turn].
4. The person goes back to the whole tree and sends nothing. No turn goes out, so no line goes out.

```
turn   map shows     first line of the turn
----   -----------   ------------------------------------------
1      whole tree    [no card is open: the map shows the whole tree]
2      card A        [the map is now at #werk-chat — ...]   (card changed)
3      card A        [still on #werk-chat — ...]            (same card)
```

card vi-routes  [decided]
Each view has its own address, so Back and Forward move between places in that view
why: With the view kept outside the address, Back in Flow jumps to the previous map card. The Back button then means nothing in any view but the map, and a reload or a shared link can open the wrong view.

Addresses:

- `/map/<id>` — the map with that card open. `/map` opens the home card.
- `/flow` and `/flow/<id>` — Flow, scoped to the whole map or to that card's subtree.
- `/graph`, `/diagram`, `/board` — the other views.

The card id in an address is URL-encoded, so an id with a colon, such as an option or a source id, makes a valid address. An address that names a card that is not in the map, or is removed, opens a page that says so.

Back and Forward move through these addresses. A switch between views adds one entry. In Flow, a row click that goes one level deeper adds one entry, so Back goes up one level (#vi-flowtab-click).

Filters, sort order, and the Subtrees row setting stay out of the address. They are display settings, not places.

A `#id` link in a card or in the chat opens `/map/<id>` from any view. An old address `/#id` opens `/map/<id>`.

The server answers every view address with the app.

The open-card line in the chat (#werk-card-blind) names the card in the current address: the map card, or the Flow scope. A view with no card in its address keeps the last card named.

I decided against the no-card line: **a turn sent from the whole tree names the home card**. The change is staged on `#werk-chat-no-card-line` and waits for your ✓.

The reason: decided cards already say there is always a card open. `#vi-routes` says the map address with no card opens the home card, and `#vi-onview` says the root has a normal card page. A "no card open" line would describe a state the map does not have. This is also what the prototype does now: your view of the whole tree sends `[the map is now at #root — …]`.
